_doc: Phase 12 Step 3 (R-P11-l6-config) - SME-editable Layer 6 constraints. Adjusting limits here is a config change, not a code change; reload requires restarting the fastapi container or hot-reloading the module. Each entry maps 1:1 onto the GeologicalConstraint dataclass in layer6_constraints.py. `keywords` and `negative_keywords` are Python regex patterns; remember to escape backslashes per JSON rules. A number is attached to the constraint whose keyword is NEAREST to it - `context_chars` is how far back to look (English names the quantity before the value: 'a dip of -60'), `lookahead_chars` how far forward (for trailing units: '1.85 g/t Au'). Keep both tight; a wide window attaches a number to the neighbouring clause's keyword and flags a correct value against the wrong constraint. Set `absolute_value` when the sign is a reporting convention rather than information. `unit_scales` (added 2026-08-21) maps a unit token written after the number onto a multiplier into the unit the bounds use — 1020 ppb Au was being compared against a 1000 ppm ceiling and reported as impossible, and 2 % Au (20 000 ppm) passed. It is unit arithmetic, not a limit change; the bounds are still yours.

constraints.name: grade_gold_max_ppm
constraints._note: negative_keywords added 2026-08-21. 'ppm' and 'g/t' are UNITS, not commodities, and _governing_constraint attaches a number to the keyword NEAREST it - so 'Uranium grades reach 4200 ppm U3O8' attached 4200 to the GOLD ceiling, because the unit sits adjacent to the number and the commodity one token further along. A normal high-grade uranium value was reported as a geological impossibility. A sentence naming another commodity is not a gold claim, and skipping is the right answer here: a wrong flag on a correct value is what teaches a reader to ignore this layer entirely.

constraints.name: dip_range
constraints.unit_hint: degrees from horizontal (0-90); sign is a convention, not a value
